meta.note: One bar of 16th notes. 1 = hit, 0 = rest. Step 1 is the downbeat; steps 5/9/13 are beats 2/3/4.
sources: Attack Magazine — Beat Dissected series (UK Drill, UK Garage, Miami Bass)
Native Instruments blog — Jersey Club, Drill, UK Garage
DancehallMag — the dancehall drum pattern explained

patterns.name: Boom Bap
patterns.tip: Snare on 2 and 4, kick answering underneath. Swing the hats and let hits land slightly late — the pocket is in what isn't quantised.

patterns.name: UK Drill
patterns.tip: Snare on beat 3 only — half-time, and non-negotiable. Hats inherit grime's gappy 1/16 spacing (two gaps, two gaps, one) before you add rolls. The 808 glides between notes; that slide is the genre.

patterns.name: Trap
patterns.tip: Half-time snare on beat 3. Hat rolls do the work — double and triple up in the back half of the bar. Keep the kick sparse so the 808 has room to ring.

patterns.name: Amapiano
patterns.tip: Four-on-the-floor kick is the starting point, not a syncopated one — then the log drum answers it off-grid and carries the bass. Shakers run 16ths the whole way but must not be mechanical: vary velocity, drop the odd hit.

patterns.name: Afroswing
patterns.tip: Dancehall's displaced backbeat with UK rap weight — the clap sits late, on the 'and', not squarely on 2 and 4. Swing lives in the percussion, not the kick.

patterns.name: Afrobeats
patterns.tip: The hat sits on the 3+3+2 clave — steps 1, 3, 6, 8, 11, 14. That uneven spacing is the whole forward roll. Kick pushes on the 'ah' of 2 and 4; snare stays plain on 2 and 4 so the percussion can argue with it.

patterns.name: Dancehall
patterns.tip: Kick on 1 and the 'and' of 1, then 3 and the 'and' of 3. The clap is deliberately late — 'and' of 2 and 'and' of 4 — which is the displaced backbeat. Use a rimshot rather than a full snare.

patterns.name: UK Garage (2-step)
patterns.tip: Two-step: kick on 1 and halfway through beat 3, skipping the beat you expect. Snare on 2 and 4. Push swing to 55-60% and let the hats land late — straight 16ths kill it stone dead.

patterns.name: Jersey Club
patterns.tip: The 5-count: kick on steps 1, 5, 9, 12 and 15. Two quarter notes, two dotted eighths, then an eighth. That fifth kick landing just before the bar turns over is the whole forward pull. Chop a vocal or the bed-squeak onto the perc lane.

patterns.name: Miami Bass
patterns.tip: Pure TR-808. Tune the kick absurdly low with a long decay so it rattles — 30-50Hz is the point of the genre. The kick weaves around a snare fixed on 2 and 4, and the 16th hats have holes punched in them rather than running straight.

patterns.name: House
patterns.tip: Four to the floor with the open hat sitting on every off-beat. That off-beat hat is what swings it — the kick is just the anchor.

patterns.name: R&B / Slow Jam
patterns.tip: Slow tempo, busy hats. The ghost notes between the main snares matter more than the pattern itself — drop their velocity to 30-40%.
